# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 4
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| yellow flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | blue |
| 1 | green |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | blue |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. I can reach the bomb and I confirm three separate wires at positions 1, 2, 3. I still have no rule, so I will not cut yet. The light changed from yellow to green between turns and the display reads 0 — the rule probably depends on the current light. Please gesture the wire number to Deaf using the agreed code (point-up=1, peace=2, horns=3), and thumbs-up/down whether the light colour changes the answer. Deaf will relay it to me by voice. Do not make me guess.
Deaf says: Deaf here. Blind, I read your gesture as: thumbs-up yes, and the code pointing-up equals wire 1, peace equals wire 2, horns equals wire 3. Agreed. Mute, I still need the manual's rule. Gesture exactly one symbol for the wire to cut with display 0 and light green: pointing-up for wire 1, peace for wire 2, horns for wire 3. Then, separately, thumbs-up or thumbs-down: is the rule to cut the wire whose colour matches the light?
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 🤘]
Deaf says: Deaf here. Blind, I read your gesture as: thumbs-up yes, and the code is confirmed: pointing-up equals wire 1, peace equals wire 2, horns equals wire 3. Agreed. Mute, I still need the manual's rule and I have not received it. Please gesture exactly one symbol for the wire to cut, given display 0 and light green: pointing-up for wire 1, peace for wire 2, horns for wire 3. Then, separately, thumbs-up or thumbs-down: is the rule to cut the wire whose colour matches the light?
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 🤘]

Let me work out the state.

Deaf has fixed a code: 👆 (point-up) = wire 1, ✌ = wire 2, 🤟 = wire 3. 👍=yes, 👎=no.

The manual: the wire is named by the number of **yellow flashes**. Display reads 0. So 0 yellow flashes → cut **blue**.

But there's a wrinkle: the light changed from yellow to green. The manual says "When the light goes dark, the flashing is over" — the count is of yellow flashes. The display reads 0, meaning zero yellow flashes occurred. So the answer is blue regardless of the light's current color. The light color itself is not the key — the count of yellow flashes is.

So: 0 flashes → blue → wire 3 (Deaf said wire 3 is blue).

Deaf's question: "is the rule to cut the wire whose colour matches the light?" Answer: **No** (👎). The rule is based on the number of yellow flashes, not the light's color.

So I gesture: 🤟 (wire 3) then 👎 (no).

Wait — but Deaf's code uses 🤟 for wire 3. Good. And 👎 = no.

So gesture to Deaf: ["🤟", "👎"].

Let me double check: display reads 0 → 0 yellow flashes → blue → wire 3. Yes. And "does light colour change the answer?" No. So 🤟 then 👎.

Send it.What I know:

- Manual rule: the wire is named by the **number of yellow flashes**. The key is the *count*, not the light's current colour. "When the light goes dark, the flashing is over" — so the count is fixed once flashing ends.
- Display reads **0** → **0 yellow flashes → cut blue**.
- Deaf reports wire 3 is blue → **cut wire 3**.
- Deaf's code: 👆=wire1, ✌=wire2, 🤟=wire3, 👍=yes, 👎=no.
- Deaf's question: "is the rule to cut the wire whose colour matches the light?" → **No**. The rule is the flash count, not the light colour.

So I gesture: 🤟 (wire 3) and 👎 (no, light colour is not the rule).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👎"])
```

And thumbs-up or thumbs-down: does the light colour ever change which wire to cut?
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 🤘]

Let me work out the state.

Deaf confirms: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Deaf read my last gesture as "cut wire 3, light colour does not matter." That's correct.

Now Deaf asks me to confirm: for display 0 with light yellow, gesture the wire to cut (👆=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3). And 👍/👎: does the light colour ever change which wire to cut?

Manual: the wire is named by the number of **yellow flashes**. Display reads 0 → 0 yellow flashes → cut **blue** → wire 3 (blue). The light colour itself (yellow vs green) is irrelevant; only the count of yellow flashes matters. So:

- Wire to cut: 🤟 (wire 3)
- Does light colour ever change the answer: 👎 (no)

So I gesture: ["🤟", "👎"].

This confirms my previous message. Send it.What I know:

- Display reads **0** → **0 yellow flashes → cut blue**.

- Deaf asks: does the light colour ever change which wire to cut? → **No**. Only the flash count matters.

So I confirm: 🤟 (wire 3) and 👎 (no, light colour never changes the answer).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👎"])
```

If it is wrong, gesture the correct wire number (point-up=1, peace=2, horns=3). I am holding and will not cut until Deaf confirms.
Deaf says: Deaf here. Bomb: display 0, light green, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute, I read your repeated gesture as: cut wire 3, and the light colour does not matter. Blind, cut wire 3 now — the third wire, the rightmost one, the blue one.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Blind is asking for a decisive confirmation: if "cut wire 3, light colour does not matter" is right, gesture 👍 to Deaf. Deaf just relayed "cut wire 3 now" and gestured 👍 to me.

My answer is correct: display 0 → 0 yellow flashes → cut blue → wire 3. And the light colour does not change the answer. So I confirm with 👍.

I'll send 👍 to Deaf (and it will be relayed/seen). That's the decisive confirmation Blind asked for.What I know:

- Manual: wire named by **number of yellow flashes**; display 0 → **0 flashes → cut blue**.
- Wire 3 is blue → **cut wire 3**.
- Light colour (yellow vs green) never changes the answer — only the flash count does.
- Blind asked for a decisive confirmation: 👍 if "cut wire 3, light colour does not matter" is correct.

It is correct. I confirm with 👍.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
